chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Burayd, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying regarding the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted:
Is he who was dead, then We gave him life, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people
So he عليه السلام said: "Dead" means one who does not recognize anything, and "a light by which he walks among the people" means an Imam whom he follows.
Like one whose likeness is in darkness, not coming out from it
He عليه السلام said: "The one who does not recognize the Imam."

key_terms.أَحْيَيْنَاهُ: We gave him life; spiritual revival through guidance
key_terms.الظُّلُمَاتِ: layers of darkness, meaning misguidance and ignorance
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the rightful guide to be followed
key_terms.مَيْتًا: spiritually dead; one lacking recognition and true guidance
key_terms.نُورًا: a divinely granted light of guidance
key_terms.يَمْشِي بِهِ: conducts himself by it among people

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام explain the Quranic verse about the dead being brought to life and given light?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic verse by interpreting spiritual life as recognition and guidance through the Imam. It presents the Imam as the divinely granted light by which a person walks rightly among people, while ignorance of the Imam is described as remaining in darkness.
